youtube.baslik: Calibrating Immittance, OAE and ABR Equipment | Lesson 116 | AIHEAR Audiology Academy
youtube.aciklama:
How is objective test equipment calibrated? In this lesson we cover the 0.5, 2 and 5 mL calibration cavities for immittance devices, checks of pressure and reflex stimuli, the OAE probe check, peak-equivalent sound pressure level (peSPL) for ABR stimuli, and the concept of 0 dB nHL.

AIHEAR Audiology Academy makes short, clear lessons for audiology students and professionals.

Sources: IEC 60645-3, -5, -6 and -7 (Electroacoustics: Audiometric equipment); ISO 389-6, Reference threshold of hearing for test signals of short duration; ANSI S3.39; British Society of Audiology, ABR Stimulus Calibration Reference Values; Hall, New Handbook of Auditory Evoked Responses; Katz, Handbook of Clinical Audiology.

This video is for educational purposes and does not replace diagnosis or treatment.

sahneler.alt: Cavities, probe checks, peSPL and nHL
cumleler: Hello, and welcome to the AIHEAR Audiology Academy.
In this lesson we will learn how immittance, otoacoustic emission and auditory brainstem response equipment is calibrated and checked.
We will look at calibration cavities, the probe check, peak-equivalent SPL for brief stimuli, and normalized hearing level.
We have seen audiometer calibration; objective test equipment must be checked with the same care.
The technical specifications of immittance devices are defined in the IEC 60645-5 standard.
In the United States, the ANSI S3.39 standard is used for immittance devices.
Otoacoustic emission, or OAE, devices are covered by the IEC 60645-6 standard.
Auditory brainstem response, or ABR, equipment is covered by the IEC 60645-7 standard.
The logic is the same for all three: a brief daily check, a measured check at regular intervals, and usually a full calibration once a year.
Full calibration is done by an authorized service technician; daily checks are the tester's responsibility.

sahneler.baslik: *What* is checked in the immittance probe?
cumleler: The immittance probe is a tip placed in the ear canal, with three separate channels.
The speaker channel delivers the probe tone; calibration checks the tone's frequency and level.
The microphone channel measures sound pressure in the ear canal; the accuracy of the admittance value depends on it.
The pump channel changes the air pressure in the ear canal; the accuracy of the pressure measurement is checked separately.
The level of the two hundred twenty six hertz probe tone is usually around eighty five decibels SPL.
Acoustic reflex stimuli are also calibrated; the ipsilateral stimulus comes through the probe, the contralateral one through an earphone.
The accuracy of admittance measurement is checked with hard-walled calibration cavities of precisely known volume.
Three cavities, of zero point five, two and five milliliters, are usually supplied with the device.
The zero point five milliliter cavity is close to the ear canal volume of a small infant.
The two milliliter cavity matches an adult ear canal and is the most commonly used check point.
The five milliliter cavity tests whether large volumes, such as with a perforation, are measured correctly.
At two hundred twenty six hertz, one milliliter of air equals one millimho, so the device should read the cavity volume directly.
At six hundred seventy eight hertz the same cavity shows about three times the admittance; the equality holds only at two twenty six.

adimlar.metin: A cavity instead of an ear

cumleler: In the daily check, the probe tip is placed in each cavity in turn and a normal measurement is started.
The volume read by the device is compared with the cavity's known volume.
A tolerance often seen in device manuals is five percent or zero point one milliliter, whichever is greater.
A hard-walled cavity has no eardrum, so the tympanogram should be flat; a peak suggests a leak or a fault.
This also shows whether the pressure system is leaking; the volume reading should not drift.
The results are recorded with the date and the name of the person doing the check.

maddeler.metin: The probe tip must be open and clean

cumleler: The accuracy of pressure measurement is checked periodically by connecting the probe to a manometer.
One device manual gives a pressure tolerance of ten decapascals or ten percent, whichever is greater.
A pressure error directly shifts the position of the tympanogram peak, and so the reading of peak pressure.
The ipsilateral reflex stimulus comes from the probe, so its level is measured in a two milliliter coupler.
The contralateral stimulus comes from an earphone, so it is calibrated in a coupler or artificial ear, like audiometer earphones.
A probe channel blocked with earwax also gives false results; the probe tip is checked after every patient.
An OAE probe contains at least one speaker and a very sensitive microphone; the emission is recorded with this microphone.
In the probe check, the probe is placed in a small test cavity supplied by the manufacturer.
The device measures the level and frequency response of the stimulus in the cavity and compares them with expected values.
There is no ear in the cavity, so there should be no emission; a response in the cavity is distortion from the system itself.
In distortion product OAEs especially, an artificial product created by the two tones inside the device can be mistaken for an emission.
So the probe check confirms that the system's noise and distortion are low enough not to mimic an emission.
In OAE testing, the most common problem comes not from calibration but from the probe tip.
If earwax or moisture blocks the probe channels, the stimulus does not reach the ear and the emission seems absent.
So a probe check is done every day; many devices do it with a single button and save the result.
In addition, a short measurement can be taken in an ear known to hear normally, such as the tester's own ear.
In this biological check, emission amplitude should be similar each day; a clear drop suggests a probe or device problem.
If the probe check fails, the probe is cleaned or replaced; if that does not help, the device is sent for service.

notlar.metin: Match the tone to the click

cumleler: ABR uses very brief stimuli, such as clicks and tone bursts; their level cannot be measured like a steady tone.
The red line shows the schematic pressure wave of a click lasting one tenth of a millisecond.
For the measurement, a steady one kilohertz tone is fed into the same coupler, and the two signals are compared on an oscilloscope.
The tone level is adjusted until its peak-to-peak amplitude equals that of the click.

cumleler.yazi: At this point, the sound pressure level of the tone is the peak-equivalent sound pressure level of the click, or peSPL.
cumleler.ses: At this point, the sound pressure level of the tone is the peak-equivalent sound pressure level of the click, or P E S P L.

cumleler: International practice uses the peak-to-peak method; measuring from baseline to peak can give a result a few decibels different.
This method is defined for short-duration test signals in the IEC 60645-3 standard.
Zero decibels nHL is the average behavioral threshold for a stimulus in a group of young adults with normal hearing.

cumleler.yazi: nHL stands for normalized hearing level; it is the counterpart of dB HL on the audiometer, for brief stimuli.
cumleler.ses: N H L stands for normalized hearing level; it is the counterpart of decibels H L on the audiometer, for brief stimuli.

cumleler: Reference values for clicks and tone bursts are given in ISO 389-6, at a rate of twenty per second with alternating polarity.

cumleler.yazi: According to this standard, zero decibels nHL for a click with ER-3A insert earphones is about thirty five and a half decibels peSPL.
cumleler.ses: According to this standard, zero decibels N H L for a click with E R three A insert earphones is about thirty five and a half decibels P E S P L.

cumleler.yazi: For example, if sixty decibels nHL is selected, about ninety five and a half decibels peSPL should be measured in the artificial ear.
cumleler.ses: For example, if sixty decibels N H L is selected, about ninety five and a half decibels P E S P L should be measured in the artificial ear.

cumleler: If the stimulus differs from the standard, such as a special chirp, building local reference values from normal listeners is advised.
In the daily check, the tester listens to the stimulus through the earphone; it should be clean, free of crackle and at the expected level.
The polarity setting and stimulus rate are also checked against the protocol at this point.
Electrode cables are inspected for breaks; an impedance check is done before every patient's test.
The insert earphone's sound tube delays the sound by just under one millisecond; the device must subtract this delay from latency.
If this setting is wrong, all latencies are systematically too long or too short, and comparison with norms breaks down.
Periodically, thresholds and latencies are measured in a few normal hearing volunteers to confirm agreement with clinical norms.

sahneler.metin: Keep cavity, probe check and stimulus listening results on a single daily chart; small drifts show up there first.
cumleler: A tip from the clinic: make a habit of recording the daily checks for all three devices on the same chart, at the same time of day.
If the cavity volume reading or the emission amplitude in your own ear changes slowly from day to day, that is a warning.
Such a trend cannot be seen from one day's result alone, but it is easy to spot on a chart.
When in doubt, take the device out of patient testing and contact the service for a full calibration.

maddeler.metin: OAE: probe check, no emission in cavity

cumleler: In immittance devices, admittance accuracy is checked with zero point five, two and five milliliter cavities, and pressure with a manometer.
In OAE devices, a probe check is done every day; there should be no emission in the cavity, and the probe tip must be clean.

cumleler.yazi: The level of ABR stimuli is measured as peSPL, by matching them to a one kilohertz tone of the same peak-to-peak amplitude.
cumleler.ses: The level of A B R stimuli is measured as P E S P L, by matching them to a one kilohertz tone of the same peak-to-peak amplitude.

cumleler: Zero decibels nHL is the average threshold of normal listeners; reference values are given in the ISO 389-6 standard.

sahneler.soru: What should a 2 mL cavity read at 226 Hz?
sahneler.aciklama: At 226 Hz, _1 mL of air = 1 mmho_; the cavity volume is read directly.

cumleler.yazi: Test yourself: with a two hundred twenty six hertz probe tone, what should the device read in a two milliliter cavity?

cumleler: The correct answer is B: about two millimhos.
At this frequency one milliliter of air equals one millimho; with no eardrum in the cavity, the curve should also be flat.
